items.description: The memory-store scenario's readiness input is under-specified. D7 has every ScriptedAgent push to its own branch `refs/heads/sim/<principal>/<change>`, and D5 says each step's `set_status` edit to `roadmap.yaml` is committed and pushed by that principal. With two principals editing the same `roadmap.yaml` on two different branches, there is no single "roadmap.yaml currently visible on the shared remote" (spec wording) for `Roadmap.ready_items()` to evaluate: storage-owner's `completed` lives on `sim/storage-owner/sim-memory-store-core`, retrieval-owner's `approved` item on its own branch, and `main` still holds the seed. The scheduler must either (a) read the dependency item's status from the owner's branch and merge per-item statuses, or (b) have status transitions pushed to `main` (modelling a checkpoint commit). Each choice changes what task 5.2 implements, what the fixture must look like, and what ri-11's flip has to touch. State the chosen ref model in D5/D7 and in the Memory-Store requirement text, and reflect it in task 5.1/5.2.
items.resolution: operator decision A1 (escalate_resume 2026-10-05) applied in PLAN_FIX fe0b333: D5/D7 integration ref = shared remote main, sim-supervisor status applier

items.description: Group 2 check: several SHALL clauses have no scenario. (a) "The harness SHALL NOT import agent-coordinator or coordination-bridge modules, SHALL NOT use HTTP or MCP transports" (Offline requirement) has no WHEN/THEN; O.1/O.2 only test behaviour, not imports. (b) "Every roadmap status change a simulated agent makes SHALL be declared as data in the fixture's step script, never in harness code" (Memory-Store requirement) has no scenario; B.1 only implies it. (c) "Registering a new probe SHALL NOT require editing any scenario definition other than its pinned expectations" (Probe Seam) is only implicit in S.1. All three are cheap to pin with a static test (AST/grep over `mpsim/` for forbidden imports and for literal status strings; a test that registers a probe without touching `scenarios/`).

Error-path reports cannot validate against `sim-report.schema.json`. The contract (exit 1) and D8 say "a report carrying a non-null `error` is printed when possible", including when "a git operation failed", and the Deterministic requirement says any scenario report validates against the schema. But the schema requires `principals` with `minItems: 2` and non-nullable `timeline`; a failure during world build (before principals exist) cannot satisfy it. Either relax `principals` to allow an empty array/null when `error` is non-null, or state explicitly that exit-1 reports are best-effort and exempt from the schema (and from D.2's "any scenario report" assertion).

Stale cross-references in design.md after the iteration-2 renumbering: the Risks table says the 30 s budget is "checked in task 6.2" (it is 9.1) and that "Task 4.2 documents the call site in the README" (the README is 8.2 and the call site is in `scenarios/blocked.py`, task 5.2). D9 says "the gen-eval pack test sets COORDINATION_API_URL" and compares reports, but plan-findings iteration 2 #3 moved O.2 to task 6.1 against raw `mpsim run` stdout. D8's exit-code table omits code 2, which the contract and task 6.2 both declare.

Re-verification of open ledger item 5: still present. The change-local header keeps the in-flight provenance note and a relative schema path that resolves correctly only from `openspec/changes/<id>/contracts/cli/`; from the promoted location `openspec/contracts/multiplayer-simulation/cli/` four `..` segments leave the repository. Task 1.1 still requires the promoted copy to be byte-identical, so the stale comment ships in the canonical file. Replace the relative path with a repo-root-relative one (`openspec/contracts/gen-eval-framework/schemas/cli-contract.schema.json`) and reword the provenance note so it is true at both locations.

Interpreter selection for the two subprocess entry points is unspecified. `bin/mpsim` "runs `python -m mpsim`"; `mpsim` imports `skills/roadmap-runtime/scripts` (needs pyyaml/jsonschema from the skills venv). Task 7.3 prepends only `bin/` to PATH and runs the `gen-eval` console script by name, so both resolutions depend on the skills venv already being first on PATH. Under `uv run --project skills pytest` that holds, but a developer running `pytest` from an activated other venv, or an IDE runner, gets a confusing ImportError or a `gen-eval: command not found`.

D5 asserts `Roadmap.ready_items()` "decides from item statuses alone" (dependency satisfied when `status: completed`, admitted when `approved`), but the architecture diagram in Context says readiness is evaluated "over the remote's roadmap/checkpoint", hinting that roadmap-runtime may also read checkpoint state. The pinned 10-tick baseline, B.4, and the ri-11 flip all depend on the exact admission semantic. The plan does not record where this was verified.

Exit-code 64 text lists "missing --fixture-dir" as a usage error, but the flag is optional; the intended meaning is a `--fixture-dir` value that points at a non-existent directory. Task 6.1 repeats the ambiguous phrase. A reader could conclude the flag is required.

`loop-state.json` records `findings_trend: []` and `iteration: 0` although plan-findings.md documents three PLAN_ITERATE iterations with 16, 8 and 3 findings. The trend field exists to let PLAN_REVIEW and escalation logic see convergence; leaving it empty hides that history from the orchestrator.
items.resolution: targets loop-state.json, which the orchestrator owns; PLAN_FIX must not edit it

items.description: The probe invocation point is stated two different ways. D4 says the driver calls every registered probe "at each principal's plan step" (which would include Alice's plan step and the plan steps of both memory-store principals), while the Same-Requirement requirement says probes are run and recorded "at the second principal's plan step". The difference is observable: under D4's wording a single stub probe would produce two `probes` entries in `same-requirement-collision` (one per principal's plan step), contradicting S.1's pin of "one entry with the stub's probe_id", and the blocked scenarios would carry non-null `probes`/`collision_detected`, contradicting D8's "fields that do not apply are null" and S.5's "appears in probes of both collision scenarios" (implying not in the other two). State in D4 and task 4.4 that probes run only at the planning (second) principal's plan step in the collision scenarios, and that the blocked scenarios report `probes: null`.

D5 does not say whether the implement step of a principal with no dependency is also admitted through `Roadmap.ready_items()` or by harness logic. The sentence "A principal with no dependency is ready at earliest_start_tick" reads as a harness-local rule, which the Memory-Store requirement forbids ("SHALL NOT use readiness logic of its own"). The choice matters for B.4: that fixture seeds the dependency item (`ri-storage`) as `completed` at tick 0, and D5 states `ready_items()` admits only items whose status is `approved`. If every principal's implement step goes through `ready_items()`, storage-owner is never admitted in B.4 (its item is `completed`, not `approved`), so it finishes with `unblocked: false` and `blocked_ticks: 47` at the default budget, and the applier would also write `in_progress` over a `completed` item if it were admitted. B.4 and task 5.1 pin only retrieval-owner's value, so the storage-owner side of that report is unspecified and a reviewer of the pinned gen-eval YAML cannot tell which outcome is intended. Decide (recommended: every principal's implement admission goes through `ready_items()`, no exception) and pin storage-owner's expected `unblocked`/`blocked_ticks` in B.4, or make the B.4 fixture remove storage-owner's implement step.

D7 declares the `Agent.act` protocol as returning `None`, but three lines later `ScriptedAgent` must "return the step's declared status transitions to the scheduler", and task 2.3 tests that it "returns the step's declared status transitions". Under operator decision A1 the return value is the only channel from agent to applier, so the protocol signature should return the transitions (for example a `StepResult` with `set_status: str | None`), not `None`.

After the A1 fix, D5 introduces `mpsim/applier.py` (the status applier) and task 5.2 implements it, but D2's package inventory was not updated and still omits it. D6 also gives clones only to principals; nothing says where the applier's checkout of `main` lives (its own clone under `<world>/supervisor/`, or a worktree of the remote), nor that its commits use the same tick-derived fixed dates and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` rules as principal commits, which D.1 byte-identity depends on. Add `applier.py` to D2 and state the applier's working copy and determinism rules in D5 or D6.

D5 says the ri-11 flip is "three fixture edits plus one expectation edit" and then lists three numbered items, of which only two are fixture edits and the third is the expectation edit. plan-findings iteration 2 describes it as "three fixture edits plus a rule change". Make the count match the list (two fixture edits, one expectation edit, plus ri-11's own rule and schema change).

Group 2 check on the Deterministic requirement: the SHALL clauses "serialized with sorted keys" and "fields that do not apply SHALL be present with value null" have no WHEN/THEN scenario. D.1 (byte-identical reruns) does not prove key ordering, and D.2 (schema validation) does not prove null-presence because the schema's `required` list would be satisfied by either null or a value. Task 2.5 does test both, so the gap is in the spec only; add a scenario (for example: WHEN any scenario report is parsed THEN its top-level keys are in sorted order AND every schema property is present, with null for inapplicable fields) and trace it to task 2.5. Every other SHALL in the delta has at least one scenario; no MODIFIED requirements exist, so nothing was dropped.

Re-verification of open ledger item 6: still unaddressed. Task 1.4's `bin/mpsim` runs a bare `python`, and task 7.3 invokes the `gen-eval` console script by name with only `bin/` prepended to PATH, so both depend on the skills venv already being first on PATH. Cheapest fix: have `bin/mpsim` use `#!/usr/bin/env python3` and have the subprocess tests (6.1, 7.3) pass `sys.executable` explicitly (`[sys.executable, '-m', 'mpsim', ...]` and `[sys.executable, '-m', 'gen_eval', ...]` if gen-eval exposes a module entry point), with `bin/` on PATH only for gen-eval's own invocation of `mpsim`. Record the choice in D3 and the README task 8.2.
